security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel context switch saves/restores vtype CSR without preserving the lambda[2:0] (bits [XLEN-2:XLEN-4]), altfmt_A (bit 9), or altfmt_B (bit 10) fields newly defined by the Integrated Matrix extension, allowing one process's matrix tile geometry or signedness/format configuration to leak into another process
security_spec.summary: New vtype CSR fields (lambda[2:0], altfmt_A/B) introduced by IME are implicit architected state that must be context-switched; failure to save/restore them permits cross-process matrix computation corruption via vtype pollution

findings.finding: Reads the full vtype CSR via csrr into dest->vtype (unsigned long), which captures Zvvm extension bits (lambda[2:0] at bits 62:60, altfmt_A at bit 9, altfmt_B at bit 10) as part of the full register word. The kernel has no explicit definitions for these bits (csr.h only defines VTYPE_VSEW/VLMUL/VMA/VTA), so the save is correct only by implicit behavior — the kernel does not know these fields exist and cannot validate them.

Restores vtype via 'vsetvl x0, %2, %1' where %1 is src->vtype (the full saved value). The RISC-V spec defines vsetvl behavior for standard V fields (vsew, vlmul, vta, vma) only; whether Zvvm-specific bits (lambda[2:0], altfmt_A/B) pass through unchanged from rs2 to the hardware vtype CSR depends on the implementation. If any hardware clears undefined bits during vsetvl, Zvvm state is silently lost — the kernel has no fallback or validation for this.
findings.snippet:
asm volatile (
    ".option push\n\t"
    ".option arch, +zve32x\n\t"
    "vsetvl	 x0, %2, %1\n\t"
    ".option pop\n\t"

findings.finding: Saves vtype correctly via __vstate_csr_save (line 202), but then executes 'vsetvli x0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma' (line 219) to configure vector register save. This vsetvli explicitly encodes only standard V fields (e8=0, m8=3, ta=1, ma=1), which zeros lambda[2:0], altfmt_A, and altfmt_B in the live hardware vtype CSR. The saved memory copy is correct, but any vector operation between this clobber and __vstate_csr_restore sees zeroed Zvvm bits.

Executes 'vsetvli x0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma' (line 255) for vector register loads, which zeros Zvvm bits in the live vtype CSR. Zvvm bits are restored last via __vstate_csr_restore (line 266), so the final state is correct for a complete save→restore cycle. However, any intermediate vector operation during restore (e.g., between vle8.v and the vsetvl restore) would see zeroed Zvvm bits.
findings.snippet:
"vsetvli	%0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma\n\t"
"vle8.v	v0, (%1)\n\t"
// ... register loads ...
__vstate_csr_restore(restore_from);  // Zvvm bits restored here

findings.finding: ACTIVELY REJECTS Zvvm vtype bits. The 'reserved' mask is computed as ~(VTYPE_VSEW | VTYPE_VLMUL | VTYPE_VMA | VTYPE_VTA) = ~0xFF, which rejects ANY bits outside the standard V fields (bits 63:8). Zvvm's lambda[2:0] (bits 62:60), altfmt_A (bit 9), and altfmt_B (bit 10) all fall in this rejected range. Any ptrace SETREGSET or CRIU checkpoint/restore of a Zvvm-using process will fail with -EINVAL. This is a concrete, demonstrable semantic gap where the kernel's explicit field knowledge actively breaks Zvvm compatibility.

The kernel defines only VTYPE_VSEW (bits 5:3), VTYPE_VLMUL (bits 2:0), VTYPE_VTA (bit 6), and VTYPE_VMA (bit 7). No definitions exist for Zvvm Integrated Matrix extension fields: lambda[2:0] (bits 62:60 on RV64), altfmt_A (bit 9), altfmt_B (bit 10), or bs[1:0] (bits 12:11). All downstream code derived from these definitions (including invalid_ptrace_v_csr's reserved mask) inherits this gap. The kernel has no symbolic way to reference or validate these bits.
findings.snippet:
#define VTYPE_VLMUL	_AC(7, UL)
#define VTYPE_VSEW	(_AC(7, UL) << VTYPE_VSEW_SHIFT)
#define VTYPE_VTA	(_AC(1, UL) << VTYPE_VTA_SHIFT)
#define VTYPE_VMA	(_AC(1, UL) << VTYPE_VMA_SHIFT)

findings.finding: Context-switch vector dispatch correctly saves prev's V state (including vtype with Zvvm bits via the riscv_v_vstate_save→__riscv_v_vstate_save→__vstate_csr_save chain) and sets up lazy restore for next. The preemptive-V path uses kernel_vstate instead and handles nesting correctly. The actual vtype preservation over a complete context-switch cycle is correct — the save captures all bits, and the deferred restore puts them back via __vstate_csr_restore.

Signal-return V-state restore copies vtype (including Zvvm bits) from the signal frame back into thread_struct.vstate.vtype as a full unsigned long. No validation of Zvvm bits occurs, but the bits are preserved in memory and will be restored to the hardware vtype CSR later via __vstate_csr_restore when arch_exit_to_user_mode_prepare runs. Compliant given the kernel's approach of treating vtype as an opaque unsigned long.

KVM guest V-state save/restore delegates to __kvm_riscv_vector_save/restore → __riscv_v_vstate_save/restore, which handles vtype as an opaque unsigned long. Guest Zvvm vtype bits are preserved through the kvm_cpu_context.vector.vtype field and restored via vsetvl on VM entry. Host V-state save/restore follows the same pattern. Compliant within the kernel's opaque-vtype approach.
